summary: OrchidLogistics: GPU eviction in dedicated pool caused partial transcript corruption and audit log delivery delay - customer escalation & post-incident action plan
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-02-25 12:07 UTC a subset of requests routed to OrchidLogistics' dedicated GPU pool experienced in-flight GPU evictions that correlated with partial transcript corruption (missing tokens/mid-stream truncation) and a delayed audit log delivery to Orchid's S3 bucket. Impact: ~11% of requests for the customer during a 14-minute window had partial transcripts or repaired replays; audit log ingestion lagged by up to 3 hours for the same time window, preventing immediate forensic validation. Immediate customer impact: downstream reconciliation pipelines flagged missing segments and Orchids' billing reconciler reported a discrepancy. Customer escalated to CSM and legal raised an evidence request within 3 hours.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-02-25 12:06 UTC: Canary autoscaler triggered a rapid pod replacement in dedicated pool (us-west).
- 12:07-12:21 UTC: Multiple GPU evictions observed; KV-prefix cache flushes coincident with evictions.
- 12:08-12:22 UTC: Streaming sessions returned truncated/missing tokens for ~11% of in-flight requests; many sessions recovered via retry but not all.
- 12:20 UTC: Telemetry pipeline started backlog; audit log delivery delayed and queued for backfill.
- 12:40 UTC: Support engaged SRE; mitigation runbook executed (pinning scheduler version, halting aggressive eviction policy, queuing backfill).
- 14:30 UTC: Bulk audit log backfill completed to customer's S3; customer notified.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Replay workload capture from Orchid prod window against dedicated pool with same autoscaler config.
2) Force a GPU eviction (simulate OOM/evict signal) during streaming KV-cache warm path.
3) Observe truncated streams and KV prefix invalidation leading to transcript gaps.

Logs / Observability pointers:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.prod/d/streaming/eviction-incident?orgId=1&from=1677320000000&to=1677322000000
- SRE trace: https://traces.redwood.prod/trace/22f4b8e
- Audit log bucket (delivered): s3://orchidlogs/2026/02/25/incident-12-07.tar.gz

Mitigation performed:
- Immediate rollback of scheduler aggressive eviction patch (rollout reverted at 12:32 UTC).
- Temporarily increased node grace window to reduce forced evictions.
- Forced KV-cache warmup disabled on eviction code path for dedicated pools.
- Telemetry backfill of delayed audit logs to customer S3 completed by 14:30 UTC.

Customer communications summary:
- 12:45 UTC: initial acknowledgement and working update sent by Support.
- 15:00 UTC: post-incident log delivery confirmation and initial remediation plan shared.
- 2026-02-27: formal follow-up with action items and credit proposal agreed.

Requested by customer: full packet of raw transcripts for affected requests, timeline of root cause, assurance of remediation, and a billing credit to cover reconciliation cost.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: aggressive scheduler eviction policy combined with a kernel selection change caused mid-token process restarts that bypassed KV-cache reconciliation, leading to missing tokens in half-completed streams.
Telemetry finding: telemetry pipeline showed a spike in eviction events at 12:07 UTC and a concurrent increase in enqueue latency causing audit log pipeline backlog.
Repro attempt: internal replay with evictions reproduced partial transcripts when cache invalidation occurred while buffer flush in serving-runtime was in-flight.
Mitigation verification: after disabling eviction-initiated cache flush in dedicated pools, replay run showed no missing tokens across 10k replays under similar load.
resolution_notes: Root cause: a recently deployed scheduler tuning (lower eviction threshold) created fast node churn under a short-lived load spike; the serving-runtime's eviction handler triggered synchronous KV-cache invalidations that could lose in-flight token batches. Fixes applied: reverted scheduler change, introduced a soft-eviction grace period, and updated serving-runtime to enqueue cache invalidations asynchronously with a recovery handshake. Telemetry: increased sampling for eviction events and added an alert for audit-log ingestion lag > 15m. Customer remediation: delivered raw transcripts and audit logs, granted a goodwill credit of $12,500, and provided a technical runbook and timeline for long-term fixes (ETA staging verification 2026-03-08, production rollout 2026-03-12).
